description: Sliding Window Attention (SWA) single-chip inference, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1. Uses 10K-token prompts (> sliding_window=4096) to trigger SWA-specific attention computation and KV cache behavior. Mistral-7B shares structural parameters with Llama-3-8B (32 layers, 32 heads, 8 KV heads, 4096 hidden, GQA) — the only architectural variable is Sliding Window Attention on every layer. Dense baseline for comparison: Suite A (Llama-3-8B at same operating point) or run Suite H with a dense model at the same prompt length. Framework support for SWA-aware KV cache allocation is version-dependent: vLLM 0.7.3 applies the sliding window in attention computation (via Flash Attention) but does not reduce KV cache memory allocation (verified via KV block count comparison). Newer framework versions with explicit SWA support are expected to show additional memory capacity benefits not captured in vLLM 0.7.3 / SGLang 0.4.10 results.
_dataset_note: Prompts truncated to 10K tail tokens from sharegpt_longctx_v1. 10K > sliding_window=4096 ensures SWA is triggered in attention computation.
_max_model_len_note: Mistral-7B's maximum context is 32,768 tokens. Suite D (30K context) uses Llama-3.1-8B with dense attention as the long-context baseline; Suite H uses Mistral-7B with SWA at 10K context to test the architecture variable.
_concurrency_levels_note: Matches Suite A for comparison. At 10K context with SWA, the KV cache per sequence is bounded by window=4096 rather than context=10000 — this should allow higher concurrency on memory-constrained GPUs when the framework supports SWA-aware KV allocation.
_request_count_note: 50 requests (reduced from Suite A's 100 due to long context prefill cost).
_online_request_count_note: 150 requests (reduced from 300 due to long context).
